items.title: ‘They’re Absolute Hogwash’: Ramsey Blacklists AmEx, a Stock Up 470% in 10 Years
items.summary: Dave Ramsey named three financial companies he personally refuses to touch, and one of them has quietly turned into a 470% stock winner over the last decade. Whether his blacklist is wisdom or a grudge depends entirely on one number hiding in your monthly statement.

items.title: Natalie Wolfsen
items.summary: Today, Wolfsen, 54, leads Orion Advisor Solutions, which provides technology and asset management services to wealth management firms and independent financial advisers.  “We can help independent advisers stay independent,” Wolfsen says.

items.title: 3 Market-Beating Stocks to Keep an Eye On
items.summary: Stocks that outperform the market usually share key traits such as rising sales, expanding margins, and increasing returns on capital. The select few that can do all three for many years are often the ones that make you life-changing money.

items.title: Can Mastercard's VAS Business Sustain Its Double-Digit Growth?
items.summary: MA's VAS revenues rise 20% in Q2, driven by security, AI and digital solutions, but sustaining double-digit growth hinges on demand and cross-selling.

items.title: How Berkshire’s New CEO Plans to Protect Iowa Power Costs From Hyperscaler Data Center Expansion
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway  CEO Greg Abel said the company will only provide power for new data centers if other utility customers benefit.  In a wide-ranging interview Wednesday morning with CNBC from Tokyo—where Abel is visiting with several large Japanese trading companies in which Berkshire has investments—the CEO discussed how Berkshire’s big utility, Berkshire Hathaway Energy, approaches data centers.
